arxiv-1802-09850.title: Solving Inverse Computational Imaging Problems using Deep Pixel-level Prior
arxiv-1802-09850.creator: Akshat Dave, Anil Kumar Vadathya, Ramana Subramanyam, Rahul Baburajan, Kaushik Mitra
arxiv-1802-09850.description: Abstract Signal reconstruction is a challenging aspect of computational imaging as it often involves solving ill-posed inverse problems. Recently, deep feed-forward neural networks have led to state-of-the-art results in solving various inverse imaging problems. However, being task specific, these networks have to be learned for each inverse problem.

arxiv-2012-10443.title: LION : Laser Interferometer On the mooN
arxiv-2012-10443.creator: Pau Amaro-Seoane, Lea Bischof, Jonathan J. Carter, Marie-Sophie Hartig, Dennis Wilken
arxiv-2012-10443.description: Abstract Gravitational wave astronomy has now left its infancy and has become an important tool for probing the most violent phenomena in our universe. The LIGO/Virgo-KAGRA collaboration operates ground based detectors which cover the frequency band from 10 Hz to the kHz regime. Meanwhile, the pulsar timing array and the soon to launch LISA mission will cover frequencies below 0.

arxiv-2108-08125.title: Multi-variant Execution at the Edge
arxiv-2108-08125.creator: Javier Cabrera-Arteaga, Pierre Laperdrix, Martin Monperrus, Benoit Baudry
arxiv-2108-08125.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Javier Cabrera-Arteaga, Pierre Laperdrix, Martin Monperrus, Benoit Baudry. Edge-Cloud computing offloads parts of the computations that traditionally occurs in the cloud to edge nodes. The binary format WebAssembly is increasingly used to distribute and deploy services on such platforms. Edge-Cloud computing providers let their clients deploy stateless services in the form of WebAssembly binaries, which are then translated to machine code, sandboxed and executed at the edge.

arxiv-2110-14376.title: simple closed geodesics in cusped hyperbolic 3 3 -manifolds
arxiv-2110-14376.creator: Feihuang Xia
arxiv-2110-14376.description: Abstract . We show that cusped finite-volume hyperbolic 3 3 -manifolds contain infinitely many simple closed geodesics. 1. Introduction A closed geodesic in a Riemannian manifold is said to be simple if it has no self-intersections, or nonsimple otherwise. It is an open question which Riemannian manifolds contain simple closed geodesics or which do not.

arxiv-2202-01721.title: Variance-Optimal Augmentation Logging for Counterfactual Evaluation in Contextual Bandits
arxiv-2202-01721.creator: Aaron David Tucker, Thorsten Joachims
arxiv-2202-01721.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Aaron David Tucker, Thorsten Joachims. Methods for offline A/B testing and counterfactual learning are seeing rapid adoption in search and recommender systems, since they allow efficient reuse of existing log data. However, there are fundamental limits to using existing log data alone, since the counterfactual estimators that are commonly used in these methods can have large bias and large variance when the logging policy is very different from the target policy being evaluated.

arxiv-2206-10828.title: Experimental Test of Contextuality based on State Discrimination with a Single Qubit
arxiv-2206-10828.creator: Qiuxin Zhang, Chenhao Zhu, Yuxin Wang, Liangyu Ding, Tingting Shi, Xiang Zhang, Shuaining Zhang, Wei Zhang
arxiv-2206-10828.description: Abstract Exploring quantum phenomena beyond predictions of any classical model has fundamental importance to understand the boundary of classical and quantum descriptions of nature. As a typical property that a quantum system behaves distinctively from a classical counterpart, contextuality has been studied extensively and verified experimentally in systems composed of at least three levels (qutrit).

arxiv-2207-00495.title: A self-contained karma economy for the dynamic allocation of common resources ⋆
arxiv-2207-00495.creator: Ezzat Elokda, Saverio Bolognani, Andrea Censi, Florian Dörfler, Emilio Frazzoli
arxiv-2207-00495.description: Abstract This paper presents karma mechanisms, a novel approach to the repeated allocation of a scarce resource among competing agents over an infinite time. Examples include deciding which ride hailing trip requests to serve during peak demand, granting the right of way in intersections or lane mergers, or admitting internet content to a regulated fast channel.

arxiv-2207-08024.title: LAVA: Language Audio Vision Alignment for Data-Efficient Video Pre-Training
arxiv-2207-08024.creator: Sumanth Gurram, Andy Fang, David Chan, John Canny
arxiv-2207-08024.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sumanth Gurram, Andy Fang, David Chan, John Canny. Generating representations of video data is of key importance in advancing the field of machine perception. Most current techniques rely on hand-annotated data, which can be difficult to work with, expensive to generate, and hard to scale. In this work, we propose a novel learning approach based on contrastive learning, LAVA, which is capable of learning joint language, audio, and video representations in a self-supervised manner.

arxiv-2303-06085.title: Propagation of light in the presence of gravity generated by static and spherically symmetric curved space-times using Maxwell equations Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-2303-06085.creator: Enderson Falcón-Gómez affil_1, Adrián Amor-Martín affil_1, Valentín De La Rubia affil_2, Gabriel Santamaría-Botello affil_3, Vittorio De Falco affil_4,affil_5, Luis Enrique García Muñoz affil_1,e1
arxiv-2303-06085.description: Abstract In this manuscript, we present an alternative method for calculating null geodesics in General Static Isotropic Metrics in General Relativity and Extended Theories of Gravity. By applying a conformal transformation, we are able to consider an analogue gravity model, where curvature is encoded in the dielectric and magnetic properties of a medium.

arxiv-2309-15937.title: The pluriclosed flow for T 2 T^{2} -invariant Vaisman metrics on the Kodaira-Thurston surface
arxiv-2309-15937.creator: Anna Fino, Gueo Grantcharov, Eddy Perez
arxiv-2309-15937.description: Abstract . In this note we study T 2 T^{2} -invariant pluriclosed metrics on the Kodaira-Thurston surface. We obtain a characterization of T 2 T^{2} -invariant Vaisman metrics, and notice that the Kodaira-Thurston surface admits Vaisman metrics with non-constant scalar curvature. Then we study the behaviour of the Vaisman condition in relation to the pluriclosed flow.

arxiv-2310-01615.creator: Stuart Daudlin 1 , Anthony Rizzo 1,2 , Sunwoo Lee 3 , Devesh Khilwani 3 , Christine Ou 3 , Songli Wang 1 , Asher Novick 1 , Vignesh Gopal 1 , Michael Cullen 1 , Robert Parsons 1 , Alyosha Molnar 3 , and Keren Bergman 1,*

arxiv-2404-17296.title: Bayesian insights in Tycho supernova remnant : a detailed mapping of ejecta properties
arxiv-2404-17296.creator: L. Godinaud, F. Acero, A. Decourchelle, J. Ballet
arxiv-2404-17296.description: Abstract Context. While Tycho’s supernova remnant is one of the most studied type Ia Galactic supernova remnants, a global view of the physical properties of its ejecta is lacking, to understand its mysteries. In particular, the spatial distribution of the Si-rich ejecta line-of-sight velocity presents a large-scale unexplained asymmetry, with the north dominantly blueshifted and the south redshifted. Aims.

arxiv-2407-21197.title: Pattern Formation of Freezing Infiltration in Porous Media
arxiv-2407-21197.creator: Nathan D. Jones, Adrian Moure, Xiaojing Fu
arxiv-2407-21197.description: Abstract Gravity-driven infiltration of liquid water into unsaturated porous media can be a spatially heterogeneous process due to the gravity fingering instability. When such infiltration occurs in a subfreezing porous medium, liquid water can readily freeze, leading to both the removal of liquid water available for transport and a reduction in local permeability.

arxiv-2501-04803.title: Geometrically simple counterexamples to a local-global principle for quadratic twists
arxiv-2501-04803.creator: Emiliano Ambrosi, Nirvana Coppola, Francesc Fité
arxiv-2501-04803.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Emiliano Ambrosi, Nirvana Coppola, Francesc Fité. Two abelian varieties A A and B B over a number field K K are said to be strongly locally quadratic twists if they are quadratic twists at every completion of K K . While it was known that this does not imply that A A and B B are quadratic twists over K K , the only known counterexamples (necessarily of dimension ≥ 4 \geq 4 ) are not geometrically simple.

arxiv-2504-09207.title: Pneuma : Leveraging LLMs for Tabular Data Representation and Retrieval in an End-to-End System
arxiv-2504-09207.creator: Muhammad Imam Luthfi Balaka, David Alexander, Qiming Wang, Yue Gong, Adila Krisnadhi, Raul Castro Fernandez
arxiv-2504-09207.description: Abstract . Finding relevant tables among databases, lakes, and repositories is the first step in extracting value from data. Such a task remains difficult because assessing whether a table is relevant to a problem does not always depend only on its content but also on the context, which is usually tribal knowledge known to the individual or team.

arxiv-2509-26641.title: Query-Kontext: An Unified Multimodal Model for Image Generation and Editing
arxiv-2509-26641.creator: Yuxin Song, Wenkai Dong, Shizun Wang, Qi Zhang, Song Xue, Tao Yuan, Hu Yang, Haocheng Feng, Hang Zhou, Xinyan Xiao, Jingdong Wang
arxiv-2509-26641.description: Abstract Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance in text-to-image generation (T2I) and editing (TI2I), whether instantiated as assembled unified frameworks which couple powerful vision-language model (VLM) with diffusion-based generator, or as naive Unified Multimodal Models with an early fusion of understanding and generation modalities.

arxiv-2510-05316.title: A New Approach to Arguments of Quantum Knowledge
arxiv-2510-05316.creator: James Bartusek, Ruta Jawale, Justin Raizes, Kabir Tomer
arxiv-2510-05316.description: Abstract We construct a non-interactive zero-knowledge argument system for QMA with the following properties of interest. • Transparent setup. Our protocol only requires a uniformly random string (URS) setup. The only prior (publicly-verifiable) NIZK for QMA (Bartusek and Malavolta, ITCS 2022) requires an entire obfuscated program as the common reference string. • Extractability.

arxiv-2602-03565.creator: Damien Morard Computer Science Department, Faculty of Science, University of Geneva, Switzerland damien@morard.me, Lucas Donati Computer Science Department, Faculty of Science, University of Geneva, Switzerland lucas.donati@etu.unige.ch, Didier Buchs Computer Science Department, Faculty of Science,

To tackle this, in this paper, we introduce a novel symbolic method for encoding Petri net markings.

plos-pone-0004010.creator: Roosa Leimu, Markus Fischer
plos-pone-0004010.description: PLOS ONE research article. Local adaptation is of fundamental importance in evolutionary, population, conservation, and global-change biology. The generality of local adaptation in plants and whether and how it is influenced by specific species, population and habitat characteristics have, however, not bee

pmc-10542385.title: FGF18 alleviates hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury via the USP16-mediated KEAP1/Nrf2 signaling pathway in male mice
pmc-10542385.creator: Gaozan Tong, Yiming Chen, Xixi Chen, Junfu Fan, Kunxuan Zhu, ZiJing Hu, Santie Li, Junjie Zhu, Jianjun Feng, Zhaohang Wu, Zhenyu Hu, Bin Zhou, Litai Jin, Hui Chen, Jingling Shen, Weitao Cong, XiaoKun Li
pmc-10542385.description: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a common complication occurs during hepatic resection and transplantation. However, the mechanisms underlying hepatic IRI have not been fully elucidated. Here, we aim to explore the role of fibroblast growth factor 18 (FGF18) in hepatic IRI. In this work, we find that Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) secrete FGF18 and alleviates hepatocytes injury.

pmc-11314965.title: Monitoring Two Typical Marine Zooplankton Species Using Acoustic Methods in the South China Sea
pmc-11314965.creator: Jing Liu, Yong Tang
pmc-11314965.description: The broadband scientific echosounder is considered to have great potential for zooplankton monitoring. In this study, two common types of zooplankton in the South China Sea, Rhopilema hispidum and Acetes chinensis, were continuously monitored using a broadband scientific echosounder. The results revealed distinct volume scattering strength (SV) spectral characteristics between the echoes of R. hispidum and A. chinensis.

pmc-12563690.title: Role of Repeat Tract Structure and the rs7158733 SNP in Spinocerebellar Ataxia 3
pmc-12563690.creator: Suran Nethisinghe, Hector Garcia-Moreno, Jude Alwan, Robyn Labrum, Paola Giunti
pmc-12563690.description: Spinocerebellar ataxia 3 (SCA3) is a neurodegenerative condition caused by an expansion of a polyglutamine tract within the ATXN3 gene. Normal alleles range from 12 to 44 repeats, while pathogenic alleles have 52 repeats or more. The canonical ATXN3 repeat tract sequence includes three interruptions at positions 3 (CAA), 4 (AAG), and 6 (CAA).

pmc-12599031.creator: Sofie Leunis, Hanne Van Criekinge, Lieze Vrancken, Marieke Vandecruys, Marie Renier, Sabina De Geest, Stijn Bogaerts, Stefan De Smet, Amaryllis H Van Craenenbroeck, Diethard Monbaliu, Véronique Cornelissen
pmc-12599031.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundUnderstanding barriers to participate in exercise intervention studies is critical for guiding approaches to increase sample representativeness, to mitigate selection bias, and to achieve the required sample size for study purposes. This study compared physical activity levels and exercise-related perceptions, including barriers and facilitators, between liver transplant recipients who were willing versus not-willing to engage in an exercise intervention randomised controlled trial (RCT).MethodsA comparative cross-sectional study was conducted using baseline data of the PHOENIX-Liver trial, a RCT evaluating a 6-month home-based exercise

pmc-12643266.title: A large-scale data set of aircraft interaction networks
pmc-12643266.creator: Raúl López-Martín, Massimiliano Zanin, Absalom Ezugwu, Absalom Ezugwu, Absalom Ezugwu
pmc-12643266.description: Complex network concepts have become the foundation of many real-world studies, encompassing topics like the dynamics of spreading processes or the evaluation of the resilience of complex systems. One of their major enablers is the availability of real data sets, on which to test and validate models and algorithms.

pmc-12650936.title: Evaluation of Digestion Methods in Microplastic Recovery from Mussels (Mytilus galloprovincialis) for a Standardised Microplastic Isolation Protocol
pmc-12650936.creator: Flavia Capuozzo, Nicoletta Cristiana Quaglia, Angela Di Pinto, Michele De Rosa, Federica Ioanna, Angela Dambrosio, Donghui Xu, Ge Chen, Lin Xu
pmc-12650936.description: Although microplastics are known as bivalve mollusc contaminants, the standardisation of isolation protocols hasn’t been developed yet. This study aims at assessing the best microplastic recovery rates and digestion efficiencies, applying two chemical reagents (10% KOH and 30% H2O2) across a wide range of known temperatures, on mussels (Mytilus galloprovincialis) contaminated with virgin microplastic standards.

pmc-12651940.title: Integrating PET and MRI Radiomics for Staging and Prognostic Stratification in Anal Canal Cancer
pmc-12651940.creator: Vanessa Murad, Andres Kohan, Lisa Avery, Claudia Ortega, Aruz Mesci, Patrick Veit-Haibach, Ur Metser, Felix M Mottaghy
pmc-12651940.description: Simple SummaryThis study examined whether radiomic features extracted from PET and MRI can enhance prognostication and staging in anal squamous cell carcinoma. A PET-derived shape feature, SHAPE_Volume(vx)(log), was a strong predictor of progression-free survival, and a two-feature model incorporating a heterogeneity measure (GLZLM_SZE) further improved long-term predictive performance.

pmc-12693821.title: SmartBuildSim: An Open-Source Synthetic-Twin Framework for Reproducible AI Benchmarking in Smart-Building Analytics
pmc-12693821.creator: Tymoteusz Miller, Irmina Durlik, Agnieszka Nowy, Ewelina Kostecka, Marco Arnesano, Francesco Salamone
pmc-12693821.description: Highlights What are the main findings? SmartBuildSim provides a lightweight synthetic-twin framework that generates reproducible smart-building sensor streams with configurable trend, seasonality, noise, drift, and missingness.The framework integrates ready-to-use AI pipelines for forecasting, anomaly detection, clustering, and reinforcement learning, enabling reproducible benchmarking across diverse building scenarios. What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-12744963.title: Farmers hold diverse and connected values towards crops
pmc-12744963.creator: Marilou Demongeot, Antoine Doncieux, Tatiana Cardenas, Anna Porcuna-Ferrer, Yildiz Aumeeruddy-Thomas, Sophie Caillon, Jonathan Locqueville, Doyle B McKey, Victoria Reyes-García, Delphine Renard
pmc-12744963.description: Considerations of yield and profit often drive decision-making in agriculture, but these are not the only values farmers ascribe to crops. Recognizing the multiple values farmers use to choose crops and their management holds potential as a leverage point for sustainable transformations.

pmc-13237291.title: Contrast-enhanced MRI improves the diagnostic performance for vaginal fornix invasion in cervical carcinoma
pmc-13237291.creator: Kailan Yang, Fangfang Rong, Funing Chu, Yafeng Dong, Hongkai Zhang, Bixiao Wan, Mingzhe Xu, Qingxin Xia, Lin Lu, Ho-Young Song, Hongmin Chen, Jinrong Qu
pmc-13237291.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the added diagnostic value of contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI) to T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) for evaluating vaginal fornix invasion (VFI) in cervical carcinoma (CC).Materials and methodsWe retrospectively enrolled 149 consecutive CC patients (training cohort) and 37 external patients (validation cohort) who underwent radical hysterectomy and preoperative MRI (T2WI, DWI, and CE-MRI).

pmc-13320586.title: The history of statistics in statistically valid regulation
pmc-13320586.creator: Christopher J Phillips
pmc-13320586.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This paper uses the introduction at the US Food and Drug Administration of dose–response extrapolation for ascertaining toxicity between 1950 and 1980 to analyse the negotiations between statistical knowledge and regulation. Those statistical methods enabled experimental results to be translated into a ‘safe dose’ of a substance for human consumption, but different methods continued to give different estimates of effects, and there was little basis for determining which methods were most accurate.
